claim: Qlinker is a novel isobaric crosslinker for studying conformational and structural changes in proteins and protein complexes.
source_text: Here, we introduce a novel isobaric crosslinker, Qlinker, for studying conformational and structural changes in proteins and protein complexes using quantitative crosslinking mass spectrometry.
evidence_reasoning: This is the primary claim of the manuscript, supported by experimental data presented throughout the paper.

claim: Qlinkers are small and simple, amine-reactive molecules with an optimal extended distance of ~10 Å.
source_text: Qlinkers are small and simple, amine-reactive molecules with an optimal extended distance of ~10 Å, which use MS2 reporter ions for relative quantification of Qlinker-modified peptides derived from different samples.
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the physical and chemical properties of the Qlinker, which are demonstrated through the synthesis and characterization data in the manuscript.

claim: Q2linker can provide quantitative crosslinking data that pinpoints key conformational and structural changes in biosensors, binary and ternary complexes composed of general transcription factors, and RNA polymerase II complexes.
source_text: We synthesized the 2-plex Q2linker and showed that the Q2linker can provide quantitative crosslinking data that pinpoints key conformational and structural changes in biosensors, binary and ternary complexes composed of the general transcription factors TBP, TFIIA, and TFIIB, and RNA polymerase II complexes.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from multiple systems tested in the manuscript.

claim: The BS3 crosslinker has a spacer arm of 11.4 Å when fully extended and can crosslink lysine residues whose Cα atoms are up to 30 Å apart.
source_text: The BS3 crosslinker has a spacer arm of 11.4 Å when fully extended and can crosslink lysine residues whose Cα atoms are up to 30 Å apart (Merkley et al., 2014).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Merkley et al., 2014.

claim: The zero-length crosslinker EDC/DMTMM can crosslink a lysine residue and an aspartate or a glutamate residue with Cα atoms up to 20 Å apart.

evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Leitner et al., 2014.

claim: 1-imino-2.6-dimethylpiperidin-1-ium was chosen as the reporter ion moiety because it is the same as the moiety used in 126–134 TMT reagents.
source_text: Thus, we decided to use 1-imino-2.6-dimethylpiperidin-1-ium as the reporter ion moiety, which is the same as the moiety used in 126–134 TMT reagents (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence_reasoning: This design choice is based on logical inference from the properties of TMT reagents.

source_text: We searched 83,242 mass spectra obtained from the analysis of a BS3 crosslinked sample of the 1 MDa yeast Mediator complex and only found 141 spectra (0.17%) containing 126.128 ions and 18 spectra (0.02%) containing 127.131 ions within a 40 ppm mass tolerance.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: The 126.128 and 127.131 reporter ions can be used for accurate quantification of Qlinker-modified peptides with little interference from fragment ions.

evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental data showing low interference rates.

claim: Maltose binding protein exhibits a conformational change from an open ligand-free conformation (1mpb.pdb) to a closed maltose-bound conformation (1n3w.pdb).
source_text: MBP is a 370 amino acid polypeptide that buries the maltose ligand between a cleft formed by its two domains and exhibits a conformational change from an open ligand-free conformation (1mpb.pdb) and a closed maltose-bound conformation (1n3w.pdb).

source_text: In both experiments, we identified one monolinked peptide (306SYEEELAK*DPR316) that was fivefold more abundant in the samples containing maltose compared to the samples without maltose (Figure 2a), suggesting K313 is modified more readily by the Q2linkers when maltose is present.

claim: K313 in MBP can form a salt bridge with E310 in the open conformation with a distance of approximately 3.3 Å, and this salt bridge is broken in the closed conformation.
source_text: Comparison of the open and closed conformations of MBP reveals that K313 can form a salt bridge with E310 in the open conformation (K313-NE to E310-OE2 distance of ~3.3 Å), and this salt bridge is broken in the closed conformation.

source_text: One crosslinked peptide was identified containing a Lys78 to Lys95 linkage, which was fivefold less abundant in the presence of CBP and CaCl2 (Figure 2b), suggesting that crosslinking between these two residues is greatly inhibited upon calcium and CBP association with CaM.

claim: Isobaric crosslinkers allow samples to be combined immediately after crosslinking and analyzed by MS together, thus avoiding potential quantification inaccuracies due to artifacts that can occur during sample processing.
